passage:
Every morning, students passed an old man walking slowly near the school. Some students became impatient because the sidewalk was narrow.
One day, a teacher told them the man had once been a marathon runner. After an accident, he had to learn to walk again.
The next morning, students saw him differently. Some greeted him. Others waited patiently or walked around him carefully.
The old man did not know why students had changed, but he smiled more often.
The teacher did not tell the story to make students feel guilty. She wanted them to understand that people's speed may hide stories. A slow step can still be a brave step.
